script.title: Post-merger EPS in a share swap
script.caption_hook: After a share swap merger, does the acquirer's EPS rise or fall?

lines.say: After a share swap merger, does the acquirer's EPS rise?
Good question. Post-merger EPS is combined profit divided by the acquirer's old shares plus new shares issued.
Target shares times the exchange ratio. That's how many acquirer shares we issue to target holders.

board.title: New shares issued
board.sub: S_B target shares, R ratio per share

lines.say: Acquirer has 2,00,000 shares and profit of ₹10,00,000. Target has 1,00,000 shares, profit ₹3,00,000. Ratio is one share per two.
So new shares are half of 1,00,000?
Yes. 50,000 new shares. Total shares become 2,00,000 plus 50,000, so 2,50,000.
Do I add the target's old shares too?
No. They're cancelled in the swap. Now add profits: ₹10,00,000 plus ₹3,00,000 is ₹13,00,000.

board.title: Post-merger EPS
board.sub: E = earnings after tax, S_A = old shares

lines.say: EPS equals ₹13,00,000 divided by 2,50,000, which is ₹5.20. Old EPS was ₹5.
Target adds ₹6 profit per new share, more than ₹5. So EPS rises.
Remember: shares in, profits in, divide.

check_notes: Writer: Example: A EPS ₹5 (10,00,000/2,00,000); ratio 1:2 gives 50,000 new shares; post EPS 13,00,000/2,50,000 = ₹5.20; earnings per new share 3,00,000/50,000 = ₹6. No synergy assumed. Check the "words" board second line fits 14 characters ("Profits in, divide" is 18).

Checker: Line 6 (voice): 'Ratio is one share per two' is ambiguous because it doesn't say which company's shares. Say: 'The exchange ratio is one acquirer share for every two target shares (0.5 per target share).' The board already says this correctly.

Checker: Lines 2/10: 'Combined profit = ₹10,00,000 + ₹3,00,000' quietly assumes no synergy gains and no merger costs. Add 'assuming no synergy' (e.g., Line 10: 'With no synergy, combined PAT is ₹13,00,000') so the figure follows only from the given data.
Checker: Line 11 (voice): 'Old EPS was ₹5' is stated without its working. Say: 'Old EPS was ₹10,00,000 ÷ 2,00,000 = ₹5.'
Checker: Line 4 board sub: 'R ratio per share' is vague. Say: 'R = acquirer shares issued per target share (here 0.5)'.
